request.spec:
The late charge now compounds: the charge for each 30-day boundary is the late percent in force
on that boundary date of the claim's figure plus the charges of the boundaries before it, each
rounded like the claim as before, then added up. A claim settled with its charge keeps the frozen
figure.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The late charge now compounds: the charge for each 30-day boundary is the late percent in force
on that boundary date of the claim's figure plus the charges of the boundaries before it, each
rounded like the claim as before, then added up. A claim settled with its charge keeps the frozen
figure.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The late charge now compounds, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

For each 30-day boundary, the charge is the late percent in force on that date, taken of the figure plus the charges already added. Each charge is rounded like the claim, and a boundary at 0.00% still adds nothing. I made the same change in the two places that work out the charge, so they stay in step:

- **Server:** `withLateCharge` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/ClaimService.java` now applies each percent to the running total instead of the original figure.
- **Front end:** `dueOf` in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/claims/claims.ts` builds the running total the same way.

I updated the doc comments on both functions to say the charge compounds.

Settled claims needed no new code: their frozen due is returned before any charge is worked out, so they keep the frozen figure.

I left the settings label ("added for every full 30 days a claim is overdue") as it was, and no stored data or schema changed.
